text:
I hear many courtiers say:

that office has three thousand reales,

but it is worth ten thousand, very exact-

God help me, and they flog Gypsies!


Those are vulgar petty thieves

who steal a cloak, some swaddling clothes,

a donkey, a mule, and their funds;

they do not amount to six Segovian quarters.


You inspect the mountains; it is a chimera,

for thieves are not hermits,

nor do they seek their career in thickets.


Let justice make inquiries here,

and it will see that the Court is a burrow

where they are nested in heaps.

translation.title: Court Thieves
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves the historical slur in context while keeping the poem's attack on elite theft.
